findings.subject: Live flow and claim limits
findings.finding: Live starts the actual finite120s frontend, records its own child PID, waits its own85s pause, then attempts session export plus both terminal/log exports regardless of early frontend exit. It contains no kill-0 or socket-liveness gate and prints cleanup_claimed=false. If the late tail is observed, it waits the frontend, clears the cached PID and preserves its actual status; export/frontend failure yields nonzero. The180s host capture/deadline is external, not a local watchdog; the comment's approximate80s startup arithmetic is not measured timing proof. Live records/PID markers cannot establish continued display, two visible windows or cleanup.

findings.subject: Closed exit and export failure control flow
findings.finding: Closed starts the60s frontend and immediately waits its exact direct child. The actual executable return, including failure after an inner successful seal/signal restoration, is retained before clearing desktop. It then attempts all five exporters even when that frontend return is nonzero: one DL22 session, two old six-file DL11 terminal exports and two DL22 application-log exports. Every actual return is printed and aggregated. Final footer/uname is reachable only after frontend0 and every export0. An inner result seal or a reaped PID alone cannot bypass those checks. Preflight refusal, pause failure or external supervisor signal may exit before exports; they remain nonzero/blocked and cannot qualify as completed closed export.

findings.subject: Ownership and traps
findings.finding: EXIT cleanup removes recursive traps and waits only stored own finite desktop/pause children. There are no PID signals or kill-0 calls anywhere. Normal explicit waits clear variables; a narrow trap race can only repeat a cached wait, never signal a recycled PID. Signal traps produce nonzero143 and wait finite owned work. This relies on the frontend returning from its own bounded policy; a hung syscall/process can still block local wait. Root's independent hard deadline and verified Linux recovery remain mandatory, including incomplete outcomes.

findings.subject: Exact export wrappers and private roots
findings.finding: Session wrappers carry host nonce plus exact phase; DL22 session uses the same nonce and records directory. Each application wrapper carries host nonce/actual derived instance/phase. The DL11 terminal span is bounded by APP_EXPORT_BEGIN and APP_TERMINAL_EXPORT_END; the following DL22 log span ends at APP_EXPORT_END. Kind/nonce/phase/directory arguments match both first-instance identities in host traces. Outer logic must partition those exact spans, retain all exit codes and reject mixed/noisy blocks; no filtering is justified. Runtime/session directories request0700 and fresh per-nonce records creation refuses reuse. Exact file ownership/modes/regular fonts remain native/exporter preflight duties; the script does not itself establish a hostile-filesystem ownership lease.

findings.subject: Nix producer source
findings.finding: The recipe pins the local PureDarwin baseline revision e7aa00a60f0b56ef35aa24252e81467787bf71ea, uses its ARM64 cross compiler/SDK and explicit native linker, and imports the page-size-fixed libSystem producer. It compiles exactly the frozen C reader path with strict C11 warnings, -nostdlib, explicit libSystem/system search paths, canonical dyld mapping, platform26.5 and chained fixups. It checks ARM64 MH_EXECUTE and exactly one libSystem load dependency, installs only the new darwin-desktop-records plus header/dependency evidence, and disables fixup/strip. It neither stages supervisors/fonts nor changes the old terminal reader. Source recipe checks do not bind the actual SDK/libSystem8ff output closure or prove execution; root's separate build/artifact report must do that. Nix was not evaluated or built by this reviewer.
